adds.title: 2017 Abu Dhabi conviction of two Singaporean nationals for attempting to resemble women
adds.summary: On August 8, 2017 Singaporean transgender woman Nur Qistina Fitriah Ibrahim and companion Muhammed Fadli Abdul Rahman arrived in Abu Dhabi as visitors and on August 9, 2017 were arrested in Yas Mall, a mixed-gender shopping mall, while wearing jeans, sneakers and long-sleeved shirts for 'looking feminine' / 'attempting to resemble women'; they were charged under UAE federal penal code article 359 (male disguised in female apparel entering a women-reserved place, punishable by up to one year imprisonment and 10,000 dirhams fine) and Abu Dhabi local penal code article 58 (violation of public morals, punishable by up to two years imprisonment and 15,000 dirhams fine), sentenced on August 20, 2017 to one year imprisonment without legal representation for being disguised in women's dress and violating public morals by appearing as women in public, held for nearly three weeks including in a cell designated for 'effeminate' detainees where guards shaved their heads and discarded Ibrahim's hormone pills, then on August 27, 2017 had sentences converted to deportation plus fine and were deported on August 28, 2017; other transgender women and feminine-appearing people were held in the same facility for solely 'looking feminine' in mixed-gender public places including malls while wearing men's clothing or work uniforms.
